predecessors.name: Indo-Scythians
predecessors.text: the Kabul-Arachosia country (51), Mathura and Sialkot (91): Cliopatria draws these in the Indo-Scythian shape

predecessors.name: Indo-Parthian Kingdom
predecessors.text: Gandhara, Taxila, the Punjab and Sindh, 'displaced' by Kujula Kadphises and his son, absorbed in 91 in Cliopatria

predecessors.name: Dayuan (Ferghana)
predecessors.text: Fergana (Dayuan): the last Great Yuan shape, 168 of whose 172 cells lie inside the Kushan shape of 51

successors.name: Eastern Kushans
successors.text: the Punjab, Gandhara, Taxila and the Gangetic plain: based in the Punjab with its capital at Taxila (Kushan Empire page)

successors.name: Western Kushans
successors.text: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley: 'soon subjugated by the Persian Sasanian Empire'

c. 51: a few edge cells of the north-eastern Bactrian growth join the Kushan shape; no page opened mentions them, so the year and the land are Cliopatria's.

c. 90: the Haryana, upper Punjab and Kashmir cells that no Cliopatria state held join the Kushan shape with the rest of the 'northwest of South Asia'.
114-120: the Kushans put their own king on the throne of Kashgar.

c. 127: the Kashgar client kingdom ends. The Shule Kingdom page (read 2026-10-19) lists 'Chen Pan (臣磐) 127' among its kings and says 'In 127 AD, Shule began to pay tribute to the Eastern Han'; it does not mention the Kushans, so the end of the Kushan relation is inferred from the change of tribute, not stated. 127: Kanishka's first year (the Rabatak inscription) and the Gangetic plain.
127: the Western Satraps are drawn as Kushan vassals (the 'early period').
150: the Kushan suzerainty over the Western Satraps ends.

c. 161: the south-eastern tip of the Gangetic gains (Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, around 'Champa') leaves the Kushan shape. Page-silent: the Kushan Empire page says only that the Rabatak text 'is not clear whether Champa was a possession of Kanishka or just beyond it'. The Huvishka page (read 2026-10-19) describes no…
225: the western half of the empire is divided from the Punjab and the Gangetic plain.
225: the eastern half becomes the Eastern Kushans, based in the Punjab with its capital at Taxila.
225: the Kushan Empire divides into two halves; the great empire is over.

wars.name: Kujula Kadphises' conquest of Kabul and Gandhara
wars.outcome: Kujula Kadphises 'invaded Anxi (Indo-Parthia), and took the Gaofu region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda and Jibin'.

wars.name: Vima Takto's conquest of north-west India
wars.outcome: Vima Takto 'expanded the Kushan Empire into the northwest of South Asia' and 'installed Generals to supervise and lead it'.

wars.name: Kushan-Han clashes on the Tarim frontier
wars.outcome: The Kushans allied with Ban Chao against the Sogdians in 84, then marched on him with 70,000 men and 'were defeated by a smaller Chinese force'; they retreated and paid tribute under Emperor He.

wars.name: Kanishka's northern Indian campaigns
wars.outcome: The Rabatak inscription claims he 'had submitted all India to (his) will'; Kushan rule reached at least Saketa and Sarnath; Pataliputra's conquest is told in a Chinese text of 472.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Kushan lands
wars.outcome: The Sasanians captured Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara in 225 (Bactria 'around 230' under Ardashir I; the east in western Pakistan under Shapur I, 240-270), replaced the Western dynasty with Kushanshahs, and claimed Kushan land 'as far as Purushapura'.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Bactrian, Indian and Tarim frontiers are inferred from cities, inscriptions and coin finds, not from lines.
